evidence.title: Christa Pike 'angry and confused' after botched execution

occurrences.checkable_against: Tennessee court order directing preservation of evidence from the Christa Pike execution attempt
occurrences.quote_span: A US judge told the state of Tennessee to preserve all evidence related to the failed attempt to execute Christa Pike, whom lawyers say is "angry and confused" after waking up in hospital nearly a week after the ordeal.

occurrences.subject: Tennessee judge

occurrences.checkable_against: Tennessee court order in Christa Pike evidence-preservation proceeding
occurrences.quote_span: The news conference followed a status hearing in Tennessee court Wednesday, during which Chancellor I’Ashea L. Myles ruled that the state must preserve any relevant evidence in connection with the failed execution.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Tennessee judge

occurrences.checkable_against: Transcript of Tennessee status hearing in Christa Pike case
occurrences.quote_span: During court, Ihnen argued that “The state has made no promises that Miss Pike will not be subject to our future execution, and the evidence that we are seeking to preserve now is relevant for any future challenge that she makes.”
occurrences.speaker: Luke Ihnen
occurrences.subject: Tennessee judge

occurrences.checkable_against: Transcript or filings from Tennessee status hearing in Christa Pike case
occurrences.quote_span: Additionally, Ihnen asked Myles to order that the Tennessee Department of Corrections give their team 48-hours notice before Pike is moved, to remove her shackles while she is in a hospital bed and to give her access to a phone or a tablet.
occurrences.speaker: Luke Ihnen
occurrences.subject: Tennessee judge

occurrences.checkable_against: Tennessee court order in Christa Pike evidence-preservation proceeding
occurrences.quote_span: Myles ultimately ruled in favor of Pike’s team, stating that Tennessee must preserve any and all relevant evidence, including but not limited to: IV lines and needles, medical supplies and records, any drugs used with anything from the manufacturer, photographs, video recordings, handwritten notes, checklists and any witness accounts.
occurrences.speaker: Chancellor I’Ashea L. Myles
occurrences.subject: Tennessee judge

occurrences.checkable_against: Tennessee court order in Christa Pike evidence-preservation proceeding
occurrences.quote_span: She said if anything has already been discarded, the state must work to “claw back that information,” and ensure going forward that no further information is discarded or destroyed.
occurrences.speaker: Chancellor I’Ashea L. Myles
occurrences.subject: Tennessee judge
